text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Monday.

LONDON - London's FTSE 100 share index finished slightly lower on Monday, depressed by a weaker Wall Street after a day spent dithering in an 18-point trading range. The FTSE closed 6.8 points lower at 4,212.0 after drifting down as the Dow gave up early gains to be 35 points weaker as London closed.

FRANKFURT - German shares end rangebound bourse session slightly lower, as activity flags ahead of Wall Street opening and key U.S. employment cost data due Tuesday. Outlook for post-bourse dealings hinges largely on U.S. The DAX index closed down 3.71 points at 2,994.53 points. In post-bourse trade the index was up 9.92 at 2,992.55.

PARIS - French shares showed their resilience, closing with a narrow gain despite a weaker tone on Wall Street. Traders said buying at the start of the February account and continued strength of the dollar supported the Paris market. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 4.83 points or 0.2 percent at 2,435.17.

ZURICH - Swiss shares ended slightly higher, but near the day's lows following a bout of profit-taking late in the day, triggered by Wall Street's weak beginning. The Broad Swiss Performance Index (SPI) added 2.90 points, or 0.11 percent, to close at 2,642.45.

TOKYO - Japanese stocks met with a renewed wave of sales on Monday, with the key market index closing two percent lower. Brokers said overall sentiment was dampened by reignited fears over the banking sectors' profitability.The key 225-share Nikkei average shed 354.46 points or 2.00 percent to close at 17,334.90.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks registered their fifth consecutive losing session on Monday, succumbing to concerns about interest rates and weak U.S. markets. The Hang Seng Index fell 84.65 points, or 0.63 percent, to close at 13,294.90.
SYDNEY - The Australian stock market is closed for a public holiday. On Friday the All Ordinaries index fell 11.5 points to 2,423.0.

JOHANNESBURG - South African shares finish barely up from starting levels, but dealers say that overall trade was positive. Expecting a weaker trend in the wake of Wall Street's Friday losses, local players enjoyed firmer industrials buoyed by strong rand, bonds. Golds held tiny gains as bullion held its footing above $353. Volumes moderate. Market eyeing Wall Street. Overall index adds 4.7 points to 6,689.3, industrials up 1.1 points to 8,043.9 and golds up 4.9 points to 1,375.3.
